summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic rectal cancer and sickle cell disease was admitted for right lower quadrant pain and obstipation. Imaging revealed a large bowel obstruction due to her known rectal cancer, with interval increase in retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy suggesting disease progression. She underwent a laparoscopic diverting loop colostomy to relieve the obstruction. Preoperatively, she was transfused two units of packed red blood cells due to anemia. Postoperatively, she recovered well, was advanced to a regular diet, and tolerated the colostomy. Pain management was adjusted to prevent opioid withdrawal by transitioning to 60 mg MS Contin three times daily with a planned taper. She received ostomy education and was discharged home with visiting nurse services, a plan to resume chemotherapy, and follow-up in two weeks.
